sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Types / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: Which part of the foot is primarily recommended for executing a highly accurate, short ground pass in football?
options: A) The outside of the foot
C) The inside of the foot
questions.answer: C) The inside of the foot

questions.question_text: In a standard competitive Kabaddi match, what is the maximum number of active players allowed on the mat for a single team at one time?
Which traditional Yoga asana is commonly referred to as the 'Tree Pose', focusing heavily on physical balance and mental concentration?
questions.answer: A) Vrikshasana

questions.question_text: True or False: In a football match, a player can be penalized for being in an offside position even if they are entirely within their own defensive half of the pitch.
questions.answer: B) False

questions.question_text: During an offensive raid in Kabaddi, which designated line must the raider cross to validate the raid if no touch points are scored?
questions.answer: D) Baulk Line

questions.question_text: Surya Namaskar, often translated as Sun Salutation, comprises a continuous cyclical sequence of exactly how many specific postures?
Which of the following is strictly categorized as an offensive ball-control skill in the sport of football?
questions.answer: B) Dribbling

questions.question_text: True or False: In Kabaddi, a 'Super Tackle' strategy awards 2 points to the defending team when they successfully trap a raider with 3 or fewer defenders remaining on the court.
questions.answer: A) True

questions.question_text: Within the core mechanics of Yoga, the practice of 'Pranayama' is primarily associated with the structural control of which physiological function?
questions.answer: C) Respiratory Breath

questions.question_text: When the football entirely crosses the touchline (sideline) during gameplay, what specific action is used to restart the match?
questions.answer: D) Throw-in

questions.question_text: Define a 'Super Raid' in the context of competitive Kabaddi scoring rules. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A Super Raid occurs when an offensive raider successfully scores three or more points in a single raid sequence, achieved through a combination of touch points and bonus points.

questions.question_text: Briefly explain the primary tactical purpose of 'trapping' the ball in football. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Trapping is a vital control technique used to absorb a moving ball's momentum, bringing it to a halt to allow the player time to execute a pass or shot.

questions.question_text: State the main structural physical benefit of practicing Tadasana (Mountain Pose) for school-aged athletes. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Tadasana fundamentally improves spinal alignment and overall posture. It strengthens the thighs, knees, and ankles while developing core physical balance and grounding mental awareness.

questions.question_text: Under what specific condition is a penalty kick awarded to an attacking team in football? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A penalty kick is awarded when a defending player commits a direct free-kick offense, such as a deliberate handball or tripping an opponent, entirely inside their own penalty area.

questions.question_text: What is the strategic significance of the 'Bonus Line' for a raider in Kabaddi? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Crossing the bonus line with one foot grounded and the trailing foot airborne grants the raider one extra point, but only if the defending team has at least six players active.

questions.question_text: Explain the rules governing a valid 'Cant' during an offensive raid sequence in a competitive Kabaddi match. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The raider must begin chanting the word 'Kabaddi' clearly in a single continuous breath before entering the opponent's court. If they lose the chant or pause for breath inside the boundary, they are declared out.

questions.question_text: Describe the correct structural technique and biomechanics for executing a legal overhead throw-in in football. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The player must face the field, keep parts of both feet completely on or behind the touchline, and throw the ball using both hands directly from behind and over their head in one fluid motion.

questions.question_text: How does the consistent practice of Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose) impact the respiratory system of young athletes? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Bhujangasana dynamically stretches the chest muscles and expands the thoracic cavity. This physical expansion increases lung capacity, encourages deeper, controlled breathing cycles, and significantly aids in clearing minor respiratory blockages.

questions.question_text: Detail the defensive strategy known as the 'Ankle Hold' in Kabaddi, and explain when it is most strategically effective. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The ankle hold is a primary corner-defense tackle where a defender firmly grips the raider's ankle. It is most effective when the raider over-extends their leading leg deep into the zone to attempt a bonus or toe touch.

questions.question_text: Analyze how executing structural postures in Yoga helps a student football player lower muscle fatigue and prevent common on-field hyper-extension injuries. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Yoga asanas build deep structural flexibility by elongating tight muscle groups like hamstrings and calves. Holding controlled balancing postures increases core stability and joint coordination. This protects the player's knees during sudden directional cuts on the pitch, while deep breath management channels oxygen to tissues, drastically reducing localized lactic acid accumulation and fatigue.

questions.question_text: A Kabaddi team is down to just two active defenders on the mat. Detail a structural defensive tactic they should employ to execute a 'Super Tackle' against an aggressive raider, and explain how positioning prevents easy escapes. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: With only two defenders, they must adopt a tight 'chain' formation, moving synchronously to trap the raider. One defender initiates a low ankle or thigh hold while the second instantly supports by blocking the upper body. This coordinated trapping denies the raider leverage to reach the midline, thus successfully securing two Super Tackle points.
